headline: ASX 200 surged 1.6% to close at 8,731 today while CBA hit a new high — but MSFT's 5.5% jump last night is the big overnight story heading into a fresh US week.

portfolio.summary: A solid day overall. CBA was the standout on the ASX, closing up 2.2% to $165.02 — a strong move for a big bank. VDHG and the emerging markets ETF (VGE) both nudged higher. On the US side (last night's session), Microsoft ripped 5.5% higher while GOOGL slid 2.5% — a real tale of two tech giants. FUEL.AX dipped slightly as oil prices fell.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Jumped 5.5% last night to $450.24 USD — a big single-session move. Amazon vs. Microsoft revenue trend analysis is doing the rounds, suggesting MSFT's cloud and AI business is pulling ahead. Strong momentum heading into tonight's US session.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Fell 2.5% last night to $380.34 USD with no major news catalyst in the data. Underperforming against MSFT in the AI race is likely weighing on sentiment.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank
movers.note: Closed up 2.2% to $165.02 AUD today — riding a broadly strong ASX session. Banks often move with the overall market, and today's 1.6% ASX 200 gain lifted the whole sector.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Up 2.9% last night to $224.16 USD. GTA-related news flow continues — Rockstar Games developers announced a union, which is a big industry moment but likely won't derail GTA 6 hype.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Slipped 1.6% to $8.46 today as crude oil fell 1.7% to $87.36/barrel. Goldman Sachs has warned energy markets may be entering a 'demand destruction' phase — meaning high prices are starting to reduce how much oil people and businesses use.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Quietly ticked up 0.8% to $76.00 today, tracking the broader ASX and global market gains.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a cracking session today, up 1.6% to close at 8,731 — a big single-day move for the local market. Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ edged marginally higher (around +0.2%), so the ASX outperformed. Gold surged over 2% last night to a massive $4,593/oz USD, while oil slid 1.7%. The Aussie dollar is sitting at 71.9 US cents, up slightly.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Marginal gain last night — essentially flat.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Flat last night despite MSFT's big move.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Gold surging — up 2% last night to near all-time highs.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dropped 1.7% last night — Goldman warning on demand destruction.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar holding firm near 71.9 US cents.

politics.summary: Three political stories worth knowing today: GDP data is due and RBA officials are speaking, which could shape rate expectations. Labor's gambling reforms are copping heat for being too soft. And Albanese is reportedly leaning on the Greens to pass a contentious tax package after an election backflip.

stories.title: GDP data and RBA speeches top the economic agenda
stories.why_it_matters: Fresh GDP (gross domestic product — basically a measure of how much the whole economy is producing) numbers are out this week, alongside speeches from Reserve Bank officials. These two things together will give the clearest signal yet on whether interest rates are going up, down, or staying put. For mortgage holders and investors alike, this is the most important local economic event of the week. Watch for RBA commentary on inflation — if they sound relaxed, rate cut hopes will build.

stories.title: 'Loopholes and deflections': Labor's gambling reform slammed
stories.why_it_matters: Labor's gambling reform package is being accused of being full of holes — critics say it lets the industry off too lightly and deflects from meaningful change. No article text was available, but the story suggests the reform isn't going as far as advocates hoped. For everyday Aussies, this means problem gambling protections may remain weaker than promised heading into an election cycle.

stories.title: Albanese banks on Greens to pass tax package after election backflip
stories.why_it_matters: Albanese has apparently reversed his position on a tax policy since the election and is now relying on the Greens to get it through parliament. No full article text available, but this signals a potential shift left on tax policy and raises the question of what concessions the Greens might extract. Investors with property or share portfolios should keep an eye on this — Greens support often comes with strings attached around capital gains tax (CGT) or negative gearing reform.

ai.summary: The big AI story this weekend is Pope Leo weighing in on artificial intelligence regulation — calling for strict international controls on lethal AI weapons. There's also a thought-provoking piece on 'meta-cognitive regulation' as the key skill for working with AI, and a couple of cheap deals on bundled AI subscriptions.

stories.title: Pope Leo calls for robust regulation of AI, especially lethal weapons
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo has published what's being described as a manifesto on AI, calling on world governments — and specifically the EU — to ban or tightly regulate lethal autonomous weapons (think: drones or robots that can decide to kill without a human pulling the trigger). He's also pushing for broader AI governance frameworks. It's a significant moral and political intervention — when the Vatican speaks on tech policy, European legislators tend to pay attention. This adds momentum to existing EU efforts to regulate AI, which could affect how companies like Google and Microsoft operate in key markets.

stories.title: Meta-cognitive regulation: the AI skill nobody is talking about
stories.why_it_matters: This piece argues that the most valuable skill when working with AI tools isn't knowing how to write a good prompt — it's 'meta-cognitive regulation', which basically means knowing when to trust the AI, when to question it, and when to do the work yourself. The idea is that people who get the most out of AI are the ones who stay mentally engaged rather than just outsourcing all thinking to the machine. Practical takeaway: if you're using ChatGPT or Copilot for work, staying critical and checking the AI's reasoning is more important than any single trick.

stories.title: Lifetime access to ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude for under $70
stories.why_it_matters: A third-party bundle is offering lifetime access to ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, and more AI tools for a one-off payment of around $60–$70 USD — the deal expires today (May 31). Worth a look if you're currently paying monthly for multiple AI subscriptions. Note: these 'lifetime' bundles are typically from resellers, not directly from OpenAI or Anthropic, so read the fine print before buying.

sport.summary: Round 13 NRL is done and dusted — Panthers scraped home in a thriller against the Warriors, the Dragons pulled off an upset over the Broncos at Suncorp, and Ben Cousins' MND diagnosis has shaken the AFL world. Big weekend all round.

stories.title: Panthers hang on to beat Warriors 20-18 in a wild finish
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith held off the Warriors 20-18 in a remarkable finish at CommBank Stadium. According to ABC, Alamoti 'made amends' — suggesting a redemption moment after an earlier error nearly cost the Panthers the game. Typical Panthers grit to win it close. The Warriors will be frustrated to come away with nothing from a game they nearly had.

stories.title: Dragons stun Broncos 30-26 at Suncorp Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: The Dragons travelled to Suncorp and knocked over the Broncos 30-26 — a big upset on Brisbane's home turf. The Raiders also beat the Cowboys 26-12 in Canberra. It was a sizzling Sunday of NRL with three games all delivering results that will shake up the ladder.

stories.title: Cousins' MND diagnosis rocks Australian sport
stories.why_it_matters: Former West Coast Eagles champion Ben Cousins has been diagnosed with Motor Neurone Disease (MND) — a degenerative condition that progressively affects the nervous system and muscles, for which there is no cure. The AFL world has rallied around the Cousins family, with widespread tributes from clubs and players. It's a heartbreaking development for one of the game's most complicated but beloved figures, and has prompted an outpouring of support across Australian sport.

stories.title: Tigers 'dodge a bullet' as Bulldogs fume over ref calls
stories.why_it_matters: Wests Tigers beat the Bulldogs 22-16 on Saturday, but it's the controversy that's making headlines. The Bulldogs are fuming over refereeing decisions they believe cost them the game, with the Tigers reportedly admitting they 'dodged a bullet'. Referee consistency continues to be a hot-button issue in the NRL competition this season.

stories.title: Rockstar Games developers announce a union — major industry move
stories.why_it_matters: Developers at Rockstar Games — the studio behind GTA 6 — have announced they're forming a union, in what's being called a landmark moment for the games industry. This is the first major unionisation at a AAA (big-budget blockbuster) games studio in recent memory. For Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) shareholders, it could mean higher labour costs and potential development delays down the track, though GTA 6's release timeline hasn't been flagged as immediately at risk.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Big jump last night — hold and watch
watch_today.detail: Microsoft surged 5.45% last night to $450.24 USD — a significant move. The catalyst appears to be growing confidence in MSFT's AI and cloud revenue growth versus peers like Amazon. No negative news. Hold comfortably, but be aware the stock may consolidate after such a sharp single-day move. Tonight's US session will be telling.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Underperforming vs. MSFT — keep watching
watch_today.detail: GOOGL dropped 2.5% last night to $380.34 USD while MSFT soared — a stark contrast. No specific bad news catalyst in the data, but the narrative of Microsoft winning the AI race is hurting Google's relative valuation. Not a sell yet, but worth watching closely over the next few weeks for any further divergence.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Goldman warns on energy demand — keep an eye on oil
watch_today.detail: Goldman Sachs has warned that energy markets may be entering a 'demand destruction' phase — meaning oil prices are high enough that consumers and businesses are starting to cut back, which pushes prices lower. WTI crude fell 1.7% last night to $87.36/barrel. FUEL.AX slipped 1.6% today as a result. No need to sell yet, but this is a developing headwind for energy holdings.

watch_today.title: RBA speeches and GDP data this week — rates outlook in focus
watch_today.detail: This week's GDP print and Reserve Bank official speeches are the most important local economic events of the coming days. If the economy looks softer than expected or RBA officials sound cautious about further rate hikes, it's a tailwind for CBA.AX, VDHG.AX and the broader ASX. Stay tuned.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Rockstar union formation — longer-term cost watch
watch_today.detail: Rockstar Games developers forming a union is a meaningful industry event. Unions can lead to higher wages and improved conditions, which raises costs for the studio over time. GTA 6 is not immediately at risk, but investors should monitor whether this causes any delays or cost blowouts in future project updates. Hold for now.
